mainTopic: How strong 'מה לי לשקר' is, then a father who betrothed an unnamed daughter: which daughters are included, and the argument between רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי about 'elder' and 'younger'.
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier discussion. A man is presumed to have brothers but not children, and he claims 'I have children.' We believe him through 'מה לי לשקר', because he could have freed his wife with a גט. רבי treats 'מה לי לשקר' like witnesses, which can uproot a חזקה, while רבי נתן treats it like a חזקה, which cannot fully uproot another one. Then a new משנה teaches that a father who betroths 'my daughter' without naming her does not include his בוגרות. If he has two groups of daughters from two wives and betrothed 'the elder' or 'the younger' but does not know which one he meant, רבי מאיר forbids every daughter the word could describe, while רבי יוסי forbids only the one at the very end of the line. The גמרא explains why the בוגרות rule is not obvious: a father acting as his adult daughter's שליח still means his minor daughter, because her betrothal is his own מצוה. It shows why both the elder and younger cases are needed, and it settles an apparent contradiction from a משנה about vows by switching the names there, backed by a ברייתא. אביי limits the argument to two groups of daughters, and רב אדא בר מתנה begins a challenge to him that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The case where 'Why would I lie?' makes him believed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא describes the exact case behind the ברייתא. We presume the man has brothers but not children. He says 'I have children,' and we believe him because he could have reached the same result with a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a case where we presume he has brothers, but we do not presume he has children. Here we say 'Why would I lie?' Why would he say this? Only to free her from the יבם. But he could just say 'I free you with a גט.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is spelling out the setting of the earlier ברייתא. It shows why the man's claim 'I have children' is believed even though no witnesses back it up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'I have children' would free his wife from יבום. But he had an easier way to free her: divorce her with a גט. Since he did not need to lie to get that result, we trust his claim. This is the logic called 'מה לי לשקר'.

keyTerms.meaning: presumed; we have an established assumption about it
'Why would I lie?' He is believed because he could have reached the same goal in another way
the brother-in-law who must do יבום or חליצה if a man dies without children
to exempt her, to release her

steps.confusionAlert: 'מה לי לשקר' does not mean we are sure he is honest. It means he had an easier way to get the same result, so he had no reason to lie.

phrases.english: where we have a presumption that he has brothers
but we do not have a presumption that he has children,
where we say: 'Why would I lie?'
Why is he saying this? To exempt her from the יבם?
He could just say: 'I exempt you with a גט.'

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּמוּחְזָק לַן בְּאַחֵי וְלָא מוּחְזָק לַן בִּבְנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion from the previous daf, defining the case of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: His claim 'I have children' is believed through 'מה לי לשקר', since he could have freed her with a גט.

steps.title: Why רבי and רבי נתן disagree
steps.stepSummary: רבי holds that 'מה לי לשקר' works like witnesses and can uproot the presumption. רבי נתן holds that it works like a presumption and cannot fully uproot another presumption.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי holds that 'Why would I lie?' is like witnesses, and witnesses can uproot a presumption. רבי נתן holds that 'Why would I lie?' is like a presumption, and one presumption cannot fully uproot another.
steps.whatsHappening: Using the case it just described, the גמרא explains the root of the dispute between רבי and רבי נתן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי, 'מה לי לשקר' is as strong as עדים. It wipes out the old presumption (brothers, no children) for good, so the man cannot later take back his claim. For רבי נתן, it is only a חזקה. It cannot totally erase the old חזקה, so a later claim of 'I have no children' brings the old presumption back.
steps.whatToRemember: How strong is 'מה לי לשקר'? רבי: like עדים, so it can uproot a חזקה. רבי נתן: like a חזקה, so it cannot fully uproot another חזקה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a clear rule for measuring how much 'מה לי לשקר' (often called מיגו) can accomplish against an existing presumption.

phrases.english: רבי holds:
'Why would I lie?' is like witnesses,
and witnesses come and uproot a presumption.
And רבי נתן holds:
'Why would I lie?' is like a presumption,

phrases.aramaic: לָא אַתְיָא חֲזָקָה וְעָקְרָה חֲזָקָה לִגְמָרֵי.
phrases.english: and a presumption cannot come and completely uproot another presumption.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי סָבַר: ״מָה לִי לְשַׁקֵּר״ כִּי עֵדִים דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the case from step 1 to explain the dispute in the ברייתא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The dispute depends on whether 'מה לי לשקר' counts like עדים (רבי) or like a חזקה (רבי נתן).

steps.title: Betrothing 'my daughter' leaves out the grown daughters
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins. If a father betroths 'his daughter' without saying which one, his בוגרות are not included.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone betroths his daughter without saying which one, the grown daughters are not included.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. Its first rule: when a father says 'my daughter' without naming her, his grown daughters are not counted among the possible brides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A father has no right to betroth a daughter once she is a בוגרת. So when he speaks generally, his words can only refer to the daughters he is able to betroth. The grown daughters stay permitted to marry.

keyTerms.meaning: fully grown daughters, past the stage when the father can betroth them

phrases.english: משנה: One who betroths his daughter without specifying which one –
the grown daughters are not included.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An unspecified betrothal of 'my daughter' does not include the בוגרות.

steps.title: 'I betrothed my elder daughter': רבי מאיר's view
steps.stepSummary: A man has two groups of daughters from two wives. He betrothed his 'elder daughter' but does not know which one he meant. רבי מאיר says all the daughters are forbidden except the youngest of the younger group.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man has two groups of daughters from two wives. He says: 'I betrothed my elder daughter, but I don't know if it was the eldest of the older group, the eldest of the younger group, or the youngest of the older group, who is still older than the eldest of the younger group.' All are forbidden except the youngest of the younger group. This is רבי מאיר's view.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה sets up a doubt about which daughter was betrothed. It then gives רבי מאיר's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that 'elder' can describe any daughter who is older than at least one other daughter. So every daughter is a possible bride and is forbidden to marry others because of the doubt. Only the very youngest daughter of all cannot be called 'elder' compared to anyone.

keyTerms.meaning: the eldest of the older group
the youngest of the younger group
forbidden to marry others, because of the doubt

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'גדולה' and 'קטנה' mean older and younger, not adult and minor.

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ שְׁתֵּי כִּיתֵּי בָנוֹת
phrases.english: One who has two groups of daughters
from two wives, and he said:
'I betrothed my elder daughter,
but I don't know whether it was the eldest of the older group,
or the eldest of the younger group,
or the youngest of the older group
who is older than the oldest of the younger group' –
phrases.notes: Literally 'older than the older ones of the younger group.' Even the youngest of the first wife's daughters is older than all of the second wife's daughters.

phrases.aramaic: כּוּלָּן אֲסוּרוֹת חוּץ מִן הַקְּטַנָּה שֶׁבַּקְּטַנּוֹת,
phrases.english: all are forbidden except for the youngest of the younger group,
these are the words of רבי מאיר.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ שְׁתֵּי כִּיתֵּי בָנוֹת מִשְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The משנה moves from the general rule to a specific case of doubt.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the case of 'my elder daughter,' רבי מאיר forbids all the daughters except the youngest of the younger group.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: only the very eldest is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says all the daughters are permitted except the eldest of the older group.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: all are permitted except the eldest of the older group.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives רבי יוסי's opposing view for the 'elder daughter' case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי, a man who says 'my elder daughter' without adding anything means the oldest daughter of all. So only she is treated as betrothed, and all her sisters may marry.

phrases.english: רבי יוסי says: they are all permitted,
except for the eldest of the older group.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי מאיר in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the case of 'my elder daughter,' only the eldest of the older group is forbidden.

steps.title: 'I betrothed my younger daughter': רבי מאיר's view
steps.stepSummary: This is the mirror case: he betrothed his 'younger daughter.' רבי מאיר forbids all the daughters except the eldest of the older group.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'I betrothed my younger daughter, but I don't know if it was the youngest of the younger group, the youngest of the older group, or the eldest of the younger group, who is still younger than the youngest of the older group.' All are forbidden except the eldest of the older group. This is רבי מאיר's view.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה repeats the same doubt in reverse, now with the word 'younger.' It again gives רבי מאיר's ruling first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same logic applies the other way around. Any daughter who is younger than at least one other daughter could be called 'younger,' so they are all forbidden. Only the oldest daughter of all is younger than no one, so she is permitted.

phrases.english: 'I betrothed my younger daughter,
but I don't know whether it was the youngest of the younger group,
or the youngest of the older group,
or the eldest of the younger group
who is younger than the youngest of the older group' –

phrases.aramaic: כּוּלָּן אֲסוּרוֹת חוּץ מִן הַגְּדוֹלָה שֶׁבַּגְּדוֹלוֹת,
phrases.english: all are forbidden except for the eldest of the older group,
these are the words of רבי מאיר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The mirror image of step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the case of 'my younger daughter,' רבי מאיר forbids all the daughters except the eldest of the older group.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: only the very youngest is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says all the daughters are permitted except the youngest of the younger group.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: all are permitted except the youngest of the younger group.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes with רבי יוסי's view for the 'younger daughter' case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as before, רבי יוסי holds that 'younger' without anything added means the youngest daughter of all. Only she is treated as betrothed.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: any daughter the word 'elder' or 'younger' could possibly describe is forbidden. רבי יוסי: the word means only the one at the very end of the line (the very eldest or the very youngest), so only she is forbidden.

phrases.english: רבי יוסי says: they are all permitted,
except for the youngest of the younger group.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: כּוּלָּן מוּתָּרוֹת, חוּץ מִן הַקְּטַנָּה שֶׁבַּקְּטַנּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי מאיר in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the case of 'my younger daughter,' only the youngest of the younger group is forbidden.

steps.title: The minors are included, so betrothal not open to marital relations works
steps.stepSummary: From the משנה's wording, the גמרא infers that all minor daughters are in the doubt. That would prove that קידושין שאין מסורין לביאה are valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: This implies that the minor daughters are included. Learn from this: a betrothal that cannot lead to living together is still a valid betrothal!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads between the lines of the משנה. It draws a big conclusion that clashes with a known opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the father has several minor daughters, each one might be the betrothed. The husband can never live with any of them, because each could be his wife's sister. Yet the משנה treats them as betrothed out of doubt. This would prove that such קידושין work, which goes against רבא, who holds they do not.

keyTerms.meaning: Open to living together as husband and wife

phrases.english: גמרא: This implies that minor girls are included,
learn from this:
a betrothal that is not open to living together
is a valid betrothal!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reads the wording of the משנה in step 3 closely
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that קידושין שאין מסורין לביאה do not take effect
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Several minors are all treated as betrothed out of doubt, even though none of them can live with him. So such קידושין must work.

steps.title: The case has only one adult and one minor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits the משנה to a father with just two daughters, one adult and one minor.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here we are dealing with a case where there is only one adult daughter and one minor daughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof by narrowing the case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With one adult and one minor, the adult is left out, so the minor is clearly the one betrothed. There is no doubt, and she is fully open to living with him. So the proof about doubtful betrothals disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here?

phrases.english: Here, what are we dealing with?
Where there is only an adult and a minor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the proof of step 8
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Many minor daughters are in doubt
steps.terutzMaskana: There is only one minor, so there is no doubt

steps.title: But the משנה says 'adults' in the plural
steps.stepSummary: The plural word בוגרות seems to show that the father has more than one adult daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה says 'adult daughters'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer in step 9 using the משנה's exact wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If there was only one adult, the משנה should have said בוגרת in the singular. The plural suggests several daughters, which does not fit the narrowed case.

phrases.english: But it teaches 'adult daughters'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that there is only one adult daughter
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The plural wording points to more than one adult daughter.

steps.title: 'Adults' means adult daughters in general
steps.stepSummary: The plural is a general rule about all fathers' adult daughters, not about this one family.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'adult daughters' mean? Adult daughters in general.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains away the plural wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה speaks as a general rule: wherever a father betroths 'my daughter,' his adult daughters are never included. So the plural does not tell us how many daughters this father has.

keyTerms.meaning: In general, of the world at large

phrases.english: What does 'adult daughters' mean?
Adult daughters in general.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The plural means this father has several adult daughters
steps.terutzMaskana: The plural describes adult daughters of all fathers

steps.title: Why would adult daughters be included at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needs to say this, since a father has no power to betroth an adult daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious! What do adult daughters have to do with this?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins: the rule seems too obvious to need saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A father can only accept betrothal for his minor daughters. An adult daughter betroths herself. So of course she is not included, and the משנה seems to teach nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: What do they have to do with it?

phrases.english: It is obvious!
What do adult daughters have to do with this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about the purpose of the rule in step 3
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the משנה to say that בוגרות are not included
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A father has no authority over an adult daughter's betrothal, so the rule is obvious.

steps.title: The adult daughter made her father her agent
steps.stepSummary: The case is one where the adult daughter appointed her father as her שליח. Still, he surely meant the daughter whose betrothal he gains from.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here we are dealing with a case where she made him her agent. You might have said that when he accepts the betrothal, he does it with her in mind. The משנה teaches us that a person does not give up something he benefits from to do something he does not benefit from.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the 'obvious' question. It sets up a case where the adult daughter really could be included, and shows why she still is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the adult made him her שליח, he could have meant her. But the money from a minor's betrothal goes to the father, while an adult keeps her own. So we assume he meant the minor, the one he gains from.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה is not obvious. Even when an adult daughter makes her father her שליח, a plain 'my daughter' means a minor. A person does not leave what he gains from for what he does not gain from.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a general rule for reading unclear actions: we assume a person meant the option that benefits him.

phrases.english: Here, what are we dealing with?
Where she made him her agent,
phrases.notes: 'She' is the adult daughter, who asked her father to accept a betrothal for her.

phrases.english: you might have said:
when he accepts a betrothal
he accepts it with her in mind,
so it teaches us:
a person does not leave aside something
that he benefits from,
phrases.notes: A minor's betrothal money goes to her father, so that is the betrothal he gains from.

phrases.english: and do something
that he does not benefit from.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Setting up a special case plus a reasoning principle
steps.terutzHavaAmina: As her שליח, he may have accepted the betrothal for the adult daughter
steps.terutzMaskana: He surely meant the minor, whose betrothal benefits him

steps.title: What if the adult daughter gave him her betrothal money?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer of Step 13. Perhaps the adult daughter told her father that her קידושין money would be his, so he gains from her betrothal too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can't we be dealing with a case where she told him, 'My betrothal money is yours'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the reasoning from Step 13 that the father surely meant the minor daughter, since only her betrothal money goes to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 said the father must have meant the daughter he gains from, and that is the minor. Now the גמרא points out that the adult daughter could also promise him her money as a reward for being her שליח. If so, he gains from both daughters, and the reason no longer tells us which one he meant.

keyTerms.meaning: Are we not dealing (with such a case)? An opening that suggests a case the answer did not cover
Betrothal; here, the money given to make the betrothal

phrases.english: Are we not dealing (even with a case)
where she said to him: "My betrothal money is yours"?
phrases.notes: She is the adult daughter, paying her father back for acting as her שליח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning given in Step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 13's claim that the father surely meant the daughter whose betrothal money he receives
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The adult daughter could also give him her betrothal money, so he gains from both, and the reason cannot pick out the minor.

steps.title: A person does not skip his own duty to do someone else's
steps.stepSummary: Even so, the father surely meant the minor daughter. Her betrothal is his own מצוה, while the adult daughter's betrothal is not his duty.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, a person does not leave aside a מצוה that rests on him in order to do a מצוה that does not rest on him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with a new reason why the father meant the minor daughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Money is no longer the reason. The new reason is duty. Marrying off a minor daughter is the father's own responsibility, while an adult daughter handles her own betrothal. So we assume he did the מצוה that was his.

keyTerms.meaning: A person does not leave aside
It is placed on him, meaning it is his own duty

steps.whatToRemember: The father is assumed to have betrothed the minor daughter, because her betrothal is his own מצוה and the adult's is not.

phrases.english: Even so,
a person does not leave aside a מצוה
that is placed upon him
and do a מצוה that is not placed upon him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ הָכִי, לָא שָׁבֵיק אִינִישׁ מִצְוָה דְּרַמְיָא עֲלֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 14
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reasoning: the father's obligation, not his financial gain, shows whom he meant
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the adult daughter gives him her money, he might have meant either daughter.
steps.terutzMaskana: He surely did the מצוה that is his own duty, the betrothal of his minor daughter.

steps.title: Why the משנה needs both the elder and younger cases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the next line of the משנה, about a father with two groups of daughters. It explains that both cases are needed: betrothing 'the elder' and betrothing 'the younger.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'One who has two groups of daughters.' Both cases are needed. If we had only the first case (the elder), we might say רבי מאיר holds his view only there. Since there is someone younger than her, he calls her 'elder.' But in the younger case, maybe רבי מאיר agrees with רבי יוסי that 'younger' means only the youngest of all. And if we had only the younger case, we might say רבי יוסי holds his view only there. In the elder case, maybe he agrees with רבי מאיר. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה. It explains why the משנה states the argument twice, once for 'the elder' and once for 'the younger.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר says a father calls any daughter 'elder' if there is a younger one. רבי יוסי says the words mean only the clearest choice. Each case on its own might seem to work only for one side. So the משנה shows that each תנא holds his view in both cases.

keyTerms.meaning: Two groups of daughters, for example from two different wives
And it is necessary (to teach both cases)
I might say he agrees with him

steps.confusionAlert: In this part of the משנה, 'גדולה' and 'קטנה' mean the elder and the younger in age order. They do not mean an adult and a minor, as they did in the earlier steps.

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ שְׁתֵּי כִּיתֵּי בָנוֹת.
phrases.english: One who has two groups of daughters.
phrases.notes: This quotes the next line of the משנה. There he betrothed 'the elder' or 'the younger' and does not know which one he meant.

phrases.english: And it is necessary (to state both cases),
for if it had taught us only the first case (the elder),
in that case Rabbi Meir says his view
because since there is one younger than her,
he calls that one "elder,"
but in this case (the younger),
I might say he agrees with Rabbi Yosei
that "younger" —
he calls only the one who is the youngest of all by that name.
And if it had been stated only in this case (the younger),
I would say that in this case Rabbi Yosei says his view,
but in that case (the elder),
I might say he agrees with Rabbi Meir;
therefore it is necessary (to state both).

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ שְׁתֵּי כִּיתֵּי בָנוֹת. וּצְרִיכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה must state the argument in both the elder and the younger cases. Otherwise we might think רבי מאיר or רבי יוסי holds his view in only one of them.

steps.title: Is the argument about putting oneself into doubt?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי argue about a general rule: does a person use words that leave him in doubt?
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean that רבי מאיר holds a person puts himself into doubt, and רבי יוסי holds a person does not put himself into doubt?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a deeper principle behind the argument. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר lets 'elder' cover any daughter who is not the youngest. That means the father used an unclear word, putting himself into doubt. רבי יוסי reads the word only in its clearest meaning, because a person speaks clearly. The גמרא tests whether this is really their view.

keyTerms.meaning: Does this mean to say...? It introduces a suggested inference
A person puts himself into a situation of doubt

phrases.english: Is this to say that Rabbi Meir holds:
a person places himself into a situation of doubt,
and Rabbi Yosei holds:
a person does not place himself into a situation of doubt?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general principle from the argument explained in Step 16
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the dispute between רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי based on whether a person puts himself into doubt?

steps.title: But elsewhere they seem to hold the opposite
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the suggestion with a משנה about vows. There רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי seem to hold the opposite views about doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we have heard them say the opposite, as we learned in a משנה: one who vows 'until פסח' is forbidden until it arrives. One who vows 'until it will be פסח' is forbidden until it ends...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה from the laws of vows to show the opposite. It begins quoting the משנה, and the opinions of רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי come in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תנאים are known to switch sides on this principle elsewhere, then the suggestion in Step 17 fails. The vow case also deals with unclear wording about time. So it is a good test of each תנא's view on doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: But we have heard them hold the opposite
Until it goes out, meaning until it ends

phrases.english: But we have heard them hold the opposite,
as we learned in a mishna:
One who vows (not to drink wine) "until Pesach"
is forbidden until it arrives;
if he said "until it will be Pesach,"
he is forbidden until it ends,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the suggested principle from Step 17
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רבי מאיר holds a person puts himself into doubt and רבי יוסי holds he does not
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה in נדרים shows these same תנאים holding the opposite positions on this principle.

steps.title: The vows case that seems to reverse the views
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting the vows משנה. Someone forbids something on himself 'until before פסח.' רבי מאיר says it is forbidden only until פסח arrives, and רבי יוסי says until פסח ends.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he vowed 'until before פסח': רבי מאיר says it is forbidden until פסח arrives. רבי יוסי says it is forbidden until פסח ends.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes the challenge from Step 18 by quoting the exact case from the vows משנה. This shows that רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי seem to hold the opposite of what Step 17 said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our משנה, רבי מאיר seemed to say a person does use doubtful words, and רבי יוסי seemed to say he does not. Here רבי מאיר reads 'before פסח' narrowly, as only until פסח starts, so he does not treat the words as doubtful. רבי יוסי includes the days of פסח themselves, so he does treat them as doubtful. That is the reverse, so the challenge stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Until before פסח, a vow that lasts up to the festival
Until it ends, literally 'until it goes out'

phrases.english: 'Until before Passover':
phrases.notes: This is still the vows משנה from Step 18. It is the next case in that משנה.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: אָסוּר עַד שֶׁיַּגִּיעַ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says: It is forbidden until it arrives;
Rabbi Yosei says: Until it ends.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד פְּנֵי פֶסַח רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר אָסוּר עַד שֶׁיַּגִּיעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quotation that makes up the challenge of Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion in Step 17 that רבי מאיר holds a person uses words that leave him in doubt and רבי יוסי holds he does not.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the vows case, רבי מאיר avoids treating 'before פסח' as doubtful, while רבי יוסי includes the days of פסח out of doubt. Their views look reversed.

steps.title: רב: switch the names in the vows משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בר אבדימי quotes רב, who says the names in the vows משנה are reversed. רבי מאיר is the one who says 'until it ends,' and רבי יוסי says 'until it arrives.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בר אבדימי said in the name of רב: the opinions are switched.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying the names in the vows משנה should be swapped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the names are switched, רבי מאיר says the vow lasts until פסח ends. That fits his view that a person does use doubtful words. רבי יוסי then says 'until it arrives,' which fits his view that a person does not. Both opinions now match our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: The opinions are switched, so swap the names

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר אַבְדִּימִי אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina bar Avdimi said that Rav said:
The opinions are reversed.
phrases.notes: He means: in the vows משנה, put רבי מאיר's name on רבי יוסי's opinion, and the other way around.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Steps 18 and 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Switching the names in the source that was used to challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The vows משנה shows that רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי hold opposite views from those in our משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The names in the vows משנה are switched, so both תנאים stay consistent with our משנה.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports switching the names
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא gives a general rule. For any vow tied to a fixed date, if a person says 'until before' that date, רבי מאיר says it lasts until the date ends, and רבי יוסי says until it arrives.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so it was taught: This is the rule. Whenever there is a fixed date and the person said 'until before' it, רבי מאיר says until it ends, and רבי יוסי says until it arrives.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that already has the names in the switched order, which backs up רב's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows that רב did not just invent the switch to escape the challenge. There is a תנאי source that says it this way, and it is stated as a general rule for any fixed date.

keyTerms.meaning: Its time is fixed, a set date on the calendar

steps.whatToRemember: With the names switched, רבי מאיר always holds that a person uses words that leave him in doubt, and רבי יוסי always holds that he does not.

phrases.english: And so it is taught: This is the principle:
Anything whose time is fixed,
and he said: 'Until before' it:
Rabbi Meir says: Until it has ended;
Rabbi Yosei says: Until it arrives.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב's answer in Step 20.
steps.raayaObject: רב's claim that the names in the vows משנה should be switched.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that already gives רבי מאיר 'until it ends' and רבי יוסי 'until it arrives.'

steps.title: אביי: the argument is only about two sets of daughters
steps.stepSummary: אביי says רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי argue only when the father has daughters from two wives. With one set of daughters, everyone agrees that 'elder' means the very oldest and 'younger' means the very youngest. A middle daughter would be called by her name.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The argument is about two groups of daughters. But with one group, everyone agrees: 'elder' means the actual eldest, 'younger' means the actual youngest, and the middle one he would call by her name.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי limits where the argument in our משנה applies. He says it is only the case of two groups of daughters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With two groups, a girl can be the 'elder' in her own group even if she is not the oldest of all, so the father's words really could be doubtful. With one group, the words 'elder' and 'younger' are clear. Any daughter in the middle has no such title, so a father would naturally use her name.

keyTerms.meaning: Two groups of daughters, from two different wives

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think אביי is changing the rule of the argument. He only narrows where the doubt exists, which is in the case of two groups of daughters.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
The dispute is in a case of two groups of daughters,
but with one group,
everyone agrees: 'elder' means the actual eldest,
'younger' means the actual youngest,
and the middle one, he would call her by her name.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי מַחֲלוֹקֶת בִּשְׁתֵּי כִּיתֵּי בָנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the vows challenge is settled, אביי returns to the daughters case in our משנה and limits where the argument applies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument of רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי applies only to two groups of daughters. With one group, 'elder' and 'younger' are taken literally, and a middle daughter would be called by name.

steps.title: רב אדא בר מתנה begins a challenge to אביי
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר מתנה starts to challenge אביי with the words 'if that is so.' The challenge itself continues in the next part of the text.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר מתנה said to אביי: But if so...
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next move. רב אדא בר מתנה is about to show a problem with what אביי just said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'אלא מעתה' means 'if your idea is true, then...' and always leads into a challenge. Here it tests where אביי's distinction between one group and two groups of daughters leads. The actual problem comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, then... It opens a challenge that tests where an idea leads.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָה לְאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Mattana said to Abaye:
If that is so,

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָה לְאַבָּיֵי אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a challenge against אביי's limit in Step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's distinction that the argument applies only to two groups of daughters, while with one group 'elder' and 'younger' are taken literally.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It uses an 'if so' argument to show that אביי's claim leads to a problem. The details continue in the next part of the text.
